source_text: תַּ֣רְתִּי בְ/לִבִּ֔/י לִ/מְשׁ֥וֹךְ בַּ/יַּ֖יִן אֶת בְּשָׂרִ֑/י וְ/לִבִּ֞/י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽ/חָכְמָה֙ וְ/לֶ/אֱחֹ֣ז בְּ/סִכְל֔וּת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִ/בְנֵ֤י הָ/אָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשׂוּ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַ/שָּׁמַ֔יִם מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּי/הֶֽם־־־׃
english_snapshot: I explored in my heart how to cheer my body with wine[a], while my heart was guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold of folly, until I might see what was good for people to do under heaven during their numbered days.

signals.text: The Hebrew is difficult and more literally says, “to draw my flesh with wine.” It may describe cheering or otherwise testing the body with wine while wisdom continued to guide the experiment.

source_text: כִּ֣י מִ֥י יֹאכַ֛ל וּ/מִ֥י יָח֖וּשׁ ח֥וּץ מִמֶּֽ/נִּי׃
english_snapshot: For who can eat, and who can enjoy[a], apart from me[b]?

signals.text: Some ancient witnesses and many translations read “apart from him,” referring to God. The Masoretic Hebrew reads “apart from me.”

source_text: וּ/בְ/כֵ֡ן רָאִיתִי֩ רְשָׁעִ֨ים קְבֻרִ֜ים וָ/בָ֗אוּ וּ/מִ/מְּק֤וֹם קָדוֹשׁ֙ יְהַלֵּ֔כוּ וְ/יִֽשְׁתַּכְּח֥וּ בָ/עִ֖יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר כֵּן עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל־־׃
english_snapshot: And so I saw the wicked buried; they had come and gone from the holy place[a], and they were forgotten[b] in the city where they had done so. This too is vanity.[c]

signals.text: Some ancient versions and a different understanding of the Hebrew support “they were praised” instead of “they were forgotten.”
